summary: Skamania County, WA lookout built in the 1930s, rebuilt in 1946 and removed or destroyed in 1968; the site lies at the edge of the Mount St. Helens blast zone.

facts.design: 12-foot wooden L-4 tower (1930s), replaced in 1946 by a 20-foot treated timber tower with an L-4 cab
facts.status_note: Second tower removed (register) or destroyed (Firelookout.com, Willhite) in 1968; Willhite reports a phone insulator, nails and an eyebolt at the site
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service; Columbia National Forest in 1947, now listed under Gifford Pinchot National Forest by Washington Lookouts

access.note: Willhite describes a gated road on the north approach and a ford of the Muddy River on the south route; no source says whether the public may enter

visit.trail_note: No tower stands. North route: about 8 miles by bike on a gated road, then a short bushwhack. South route: from the Smith Creek Butte Trailhead, a ford of the Muddy River, then a trail Willhite says should exist

events.note: Shows as a lookout station on the 1932 USFS map; start date unknown (Willhite)
First lookout dismantled and rebuilt about 30 feet north as a 20-foot treated timber tower with an L-4 cab
About 4,000 pounds of building materials flown in by airplane, per a Forest Log article quoted by Willhite and Washington Lookouts
Second tower and cab removed (register) or destroyed (Firelookout.com, Willhite)
USGS Geodimeter station set up at the site just before the eruption; photo dated April 25, 1980

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says removed in 1968; Firelookout.com says destroyed in 1968; Willhite says removed or destroyed. All agree on 1968.

resolved_conflicts.field: start date of the first tower
resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register and Firelookout.com say the 1930s; Willhite says the site appears on a 1932 map and does not know the start date.

sources.title: Smith Creek Butte Fire Lookout Tower

notes_for_editor: Gone status and 1946 and 1968 dates agree across sources. Remains, the 2023 visit and the routes rest on Willhite alone. The restricted access level is inferred from the 'gated road' wording; no source states public status. The 1947 airlift is second-hand through Willhite and Washington Lookouts.
